paper_metadata.title: Antiepileptic drugs withdrawal in patients with idiopathic generalized epilepsy

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study uses a consecutive sample from referral centers with clear inclusion criteria and baseline descriptions. However, it explicitly excludes 'non-responders' and those with missing data, which may introduce selection bias by only including patients with better follow-up adherence or clearer clinical profiles.

items.label: Source of target population
items.prompt: The source population or population of interest is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: consecutive patients from two regional referral University hospitals: Institute for Child and Adolescents Health Care in Novi Sad and Clinic for Neurology and Psychiatry for Children and Youth in Belgrade, Serbia
items.reasoning: The authors clearly define the geographic and institutional source of the patients.

items.label: Method used to identify population
items.prompt: The sampling frame and recruitment are adequately described, including methods to identify the sample sufficient to limit potential bias (number and type used, e.g., referral patterns in health care)
items.evidence_snippet: Subjects were identified among consecutive patients... Patients who dropped out of the follow up from different reasons – non-responders or attending other Clinics were not included.
items.reasoning: While recruitment was consecutive, the exclusion of 'non-responders' without further detail suggests a potential selection bias toward compliant patients.

items.label: Recruitment period
items.prompt: Period of recruitment is adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: The study was conducted from June 2001 through December 2009.
items.reasoning: The dates for the study period are explicitly stated.

items.label: Place of recruitment
items.prompt: Place of recruitment (setting and geographic location)  are adequately described
items.evidence_snippet: two regional referral University hospitals: Institute for Child and Adolescents Health Care in Novi Sad and Clinic for Neurology and Psychiatry for Children and Youth in Belgrade, Serbia (85 km apart from each other).
items.reasoning: Specific hospital names and locations are provided.

items.label: Inclusion and exclusion criteria
items.prompt: Inclusion and exclusion criteria are adequately described (e.g., including explicit diagnostic criteria or “zero time” description).
items.evidence_snippet: Inclusion criteria were: diagnosis of IGE according to the ILAE criteria, established clinical remission of at least two years before AED withdrawal and clinical follow up for at least two years after withdrawal or until seizure relapse.
items.reasoning: Criteria include diagnostic standards (ILAE), duration of remission, and follow-up requirements.

items.label: Adequate study participation
items.prompt: There is adequate participation in the study by eligible individuals
items.evidence_snippet: Not found in text

items.label: Baseline characteristics
items.prompt: The baseline study sample (i.e., individuals entering the study) is adequately described for key characteristics (LIST).
items.evidence_snippet: The distribution was as follows: childhood absence epilepsy (CAE) in 21 (35.6%) patients; juvenile absence epilepsy (JAE) in 11 (18.6%) patients, epilepsy with primary GTC seizures in 10 (16.9%) patients, and juvenile myoclonic epilepsy (JME) in remaining 17 (28.8%) patients.
items.reasoning: Table 3 and the text provide detailed baseline data on age, sex, syndrome type, and EEG findings.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study excludes patients who dropped out or had missing data from the initial cohort rather than accounting for them in the analysis. Furthermore, 15 patients were excluded from the primary analysis because they had 'EEG worsening' and restarted meds, which is a form of informative censoring that likely underestimates the true relapse risk.

items.label: Proportion of baseline sample available for analysis
items.prompt: Response rate (i.e., proportion of study sample completing the study and providing outcome data) is adequate.
items.evidence_snippet: Patients who dropped out of the follow up from different reasons – non-responders or attending other Clinics were not included... This group of patients [EEG worsening], therefore, was excluded from the estimation of risk for seizure recurrence.
items.reasoning: A significant portion of the cohort (15/59) was excluded post-hoc due to clinical decisions (restarting AEDs), and dropouts were excluded entirely.

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Attrition Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Loss to follow-up (from baseline sample to study population analyzed) is not associated with key characteristics (i.e., the study data adequately represent the sample) sufficient to limit potential bias to the observed relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: Prognostic factors (syndrome type, EEG features) are well-defined and measured using standard clinical protocols (ILAE criteria and 10-20 EEG system).

items.label: Definition of the PF
items.prompt: A clear definition or description of 'PF' is provided (e.g., including dose, level, duration of exposure, and clear specification of the method of measurement).
items.evidence_snippet: The following variables, derived from the case records were analyzed: ... age at seizure onset, type of seizure, ... EEGs registered before, during and after AED withdrawal
items.reasoning: The prognostic factors are clearly listed and defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of PF

items.evidence_snippet: EEG in both settings was recorded according to the international 10–20 electrode placement system (21 channel) using Oxford Medilec EEG machine.
items.reasoning: Standardized, objective equipment and protocols were used for the primary prognostic factor (EEG).

items.prompt: Continuous variables are reported or appropriate cut-points (i.e., not data-dependent) are used.
items.evidence_snippet: age at seizure onset above 10 years... age of AED withdrawal above 15 years.
items.reasoning: Cut-points are used for age, but it is not explicitly stated if these were pre-specified or determined based on the data (data-dependent).

items.evidence_snippet: EEG in both settings was recorded according to the international 10–20 electrode placement system
items.reasoning: The protocol was standardized across both hospital sites.

items.evidence_snippet: Patients were not eligible for the study ... if all needed relevant data were not available from the case history notes.

items.reasoning: The outcome is clearly defined as clinical seizure recurrence.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Outcome

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Outcome Measurement Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Outcome of interest is adequately measured in study participants to sufficiently limit potential bias.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The study accounts for several confounders in a multivariable Cox model. However, the exclusion of the 15 patients who restarted AEDs due to EEG worsening is a major confounding-by-indication issue that was not statistically addressed.

items.label: Important Confounders Measured
items.prompt: All important confounders, including treatments (key variables in conceptual model: LIST), are measured.
items.evidence_snippet: The following variables, derived from the case records were analyzed: ... age and sex, age at seizure onset, type of seizure, cognitive and neurological status, history of status epilepticus, EEGs... AED in monotherapy vs. polytherapy, length of AED therapy
items.reasoning: A comprehensive list of clinical and demographic confounders was collected.

items.label: Definition of the confounding factor
items.prompt: Clear definitions of the important confounders measured are provided (e.g., including dose, level, and duration of exposures).
items.evidence_snippet: The AED therapy duration was in range 1–9 years (median 4). The length of stable clinical remission while on AED was in range 2.5–9 years (median 4).
items.reasoning: Confounders like treatment duration and remission length are clearly defined.

items.label: Valid and Reliable Measurement of Confounders
items.prompt: Measurement of all important confounders is adequately valid and reliable (e.g., may include relevant outside sources of information on measurement properties, also characteristics, such as blind measurement and limited reliance on recall).
items.evidence_snippet: Medical records of patients coded as IGE were evaluated during the observational period.
items.reasoning: Data were extracted from formal medical records, which is generally reliable for clinical variables.

items.label: Method and Setting of Confounding Measurement
items.prompt: The method and setting of confounding measurement are the same for all study participants.
items.evidence_snippet: These variables entered computerized database formed for all out-patients regularly examined.
items.reasoning: A uniform database and examination protocol were used.

items.prompt: Important potential confounders are accounted for in the analysis (i.e., appropriate adjustment).

risk_of_bias_assessment.label: Study Confounding Summary
risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: Important potential confounders are appropriately accounted for, limiting potential bias with respect to the relationship between PF and outcome.

quips_assessment.risk_reasoning: The statistical methods (Kaplan-Meier, Cox regression) are appropriate for time-to-event data. However, the sample size is small (n=44 for the final analysis), which limits the power of the multivariate model and increases the risk of overfitting.

items.label: Presentation of analytical strategy
items.prompt: There is sufficient presentation of data to assess the adequacy of the analysis.
items.evidence_snippet: time to seizure relapse was analyzed by Kaplan Meir method... Relative risks for recurrence during the follow-up were investigated by Cox regression analysis
items.reasoning: The strategy is standard and well-described.

items.label: Model development strategy
items.prompt: The strategy for model building (i.e., inclusion of variables in the statistical model) is appropriate and is based on a conceptual framework or model.
items.evidence_snippet: Factors of possible prognostic values were evaluated by x2 test... Multivariate analysis was applied in order to investigate the simultaneous influence of several factors
items.reasoning: The authors used univariate significance to select variables for the multivariate model, which is a common but sometimes criticized strategy compared to purely conceptual modeling.

items.prompt: The selected statistical model is adequate for the design of the study.
items.evidence_snippet: SPSS software package for statistical analysis was used... Cox regression analysis – uni/ multivariate analyses to allow for variable length of follow up.
items.reasoning: Cox regression is the correct choice for survival data with varying follow-up lengths.

items.label: Reporting of results

items.evidence_snippet: Table 3, 4, and 5
items.reasoning: The authors report both significant and non-significant findings for all measured variables.

risk_of_bias_assessment.prompt: The statistical analysis is appropriate for the design of the study, limiting potential for presentation of invalid or spurious results.
